G4500.def:
ῥοιζηδόν 
adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow), 
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2 Pierre 3:10.†

G4501.def:
ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;] 
a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Apocalypse 1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Luc 2:35.†

G4502.def:
Ῥουβήν, ὁ indecl., (Heb. רְאוּבֵן), 
Reuben: Apocalypse 7:5.†

G4503.def:
Ῥoύθ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רוּת), 
Ruth: Matthieu 15:1-39.†

G4505.def:
ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 15:3 (רְחֹב), Proverbes 31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;] 
__1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers. 
__2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Matthieu 6:2, Luc 14:21 Actes 9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).†

G4506.def:
ῥύομαι 
[in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi., also for גָּאַל, פָּלַט pi., etc. ;] 
to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 27:43, 2 Pierre 2:7; id. before ἀπό, Matthieu 6:13, Luc 11:4 (Rec., R, mg.), 2 Timothée 4:18; before ἐκ, Romains 7:24, 2 Corinthiens 1:10, Colossiens 1:13, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:10, 2 Timothée 3:11, 2 Pierre 2:9; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, Romains 11:26. Passive: before ἀπό, Romains 15:31, 2 Thessaloniciens 3:2; before ἐκ, Luc 1:74, 2 Timothée 4:17.†

G4507.def:
ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ
(ῥυπαρός) 
filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, Jacques 1:21.†

G4508.def:
ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν
(ῥύπος), [in LXX: Zacharie 3:4-5, (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;] 
filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Jacques 2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Apocalypse 22:11.†

G4509.def:
ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 4:4 (צוֹאָה), Job 14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;] 
dirt, filth: 1 Pierre 3:21.†

G4510.def:
ῥυπόω, -ῶ 
(ῥύπος), 
to make filthy: Apocalypse 22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†

G4511.def:
ῥύσις, -εως, ἡ
(ῥέω), [in LXX chiefly for זוֹב ;] 
a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, Marc 5:25, Luc 8:43-44.†

G4512.def: a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G4513.def:
Roman, a Roman , (Polybius Historicus), etc.; adverb -κῶς, in Latin , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
(ML)

G4514.def:
Ῥωμαῖος, -α, -ον 
Roman: Jean 11:48, Actes 2:10 (RV, from Rome), Actes 16:21, 37-38 22:25-27, 29 23:27 25:16 28:17.†

G4516.def:
Ῥώμη, -ης, ἡ
Rome: Actes 18:2 19:21 23:11 28:14, 16 Romains 1:7, 15, 2 Timothée 1:17.†

G4517.def:
ῥώννυμι
[in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;] 
to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Actes 15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†

G4518.def:
σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי), 
sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Matthieu 27:46, Marc 15:34 (Psaumes 22:2, Heb. עָזַב).†
ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב), 
zaphthanei: Matthieu 27:46 (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).†

G4519.def:
σαβαώθ indecl., 
[in LXX for צָבָא, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; see DB, iii, 137 f.) ;] 
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): Romains 9:29 (LXX), Ja 54.†

G4520.def:
σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Exode 16:30, al.), 
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), Hébreux 4:9.†

G4522.def:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;] 
a drag-net, seine: Matthieu 13:47.†
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον

G4523.def:
Σαδδουκαῖος, -ου, ὁ
(Heb. צָדוֹק, 2 Rois 15:24, al.), 
a Sadducee (cf. Swete, Mk., 277): Matthieu 3:7 16:1, 6 16:11-12 22:23-34 Marc 12:18, Luc 20:27, Actes 4:1 5:17 23:6-8.†

G4524.def:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος) 
Sadoc, Zadok: Matthieu 1:14.†

G4525.def:
σαίνω 
__1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn. 
__2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1 Thessaloniciens 3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†

G4527G.def:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), 
Sala, Shalah: Luc 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luc 3:35.†

G4527H.def:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח), 
Sala, Shalah: Luc 3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luc 3:35.†

G4528G.def:
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ 
indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל), 
Salathiel: Matthieu 1:12, Luc 3:27.†

G4528H.def:
Σαλαθιήλ, ὁ 
indecl. (Heb. שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל), 
Salathiel: Matthieu 1:12, Luc 3:27.†

G4529.def:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνσς, ἡ 
Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Actes 13:5.†

G4530.def:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl., 
Salim: Jean 3:23 (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).†

G4532.def:
Σαλήμ, ἡ (Heb. שָׁלֵם Genèse 14:18), 
Salem: Hébreux 7:1-2 (LXX).†

G4533.def:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן), 
Salmon: Matthieu 1:4-5, Luc 3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†

G4534.def:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ 
Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Actes 27:7.†

G4535.def:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;] 
in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Luc 21:25.†

G4536.def:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;] 
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1 Corinthiens 14:8, Hébreux 12:19, Apocalypse 1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Matthieu 24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1 Corinthiens 15:52.†

G4537.def:
σαλπίζω 
[in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;] 
to sound a trumpet: Apocalypse 8:6 ff. Apocalypse 9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Matthieu 6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1 Corinthiens 15:52.†

G4538.def:
σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ, 
a trumpeter: Apocalypse 18:22.†

G4541.def:
Σαμαρείτης
(-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, 
a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Matthieu 10:5, Luc 9:52 10:33 17:16, Jean 4:9, 39-40, Actes 8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jean 8:48.†

G4542.def:
Σαμαρεῖτις (-ῖτις, T, see supr.), -ιδος, ἡ 
__1. in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria. 
__2. a Samaritan woman: Jean 4:9.†

G4543.def:
Σαμοθρᾴκη
(-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ 
Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: Actes 16:11.†

G4544.def:
Σάμος, -ου, ἡ 
Samos, an island in the Ægean: Actes 20:15.†

G4545.def:
Σαμουήλ, ὁ indecl. 
(in FlJ, Σαμούηλος; Heb. שְׁמוּאֵל), 
Samuel (1 Rois 1:20, al.): Actes 3:24 13:20, Hébreux 11:32.†

G4546.def:
Σαμψών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שִׁמְשׁוֹן), 
Samson (Juges 13:1-25 ff.): Hébreux 11:32.†

G4547.def:
σανδάλιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σάνδαλον, prob. Persian), [in LXX: Josué 9:5, Ésaïe 20:2 (נָעַל, elsewhere rendered ὑπόδημα, which see), Jdth.10:4 16:9 * ;] 
a sandal: Marc 6:9, Actes 12:8.†

G4548.def:
σανίς, -ίδος, ἡ 
[in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 8:9, Eze.27:5 (לוּחַ) * ;] 
a board, plank: Actes 27:44

G4550.def:
σαπρός, -ά -όν 
[in Sm.: Lévitique 27:14, 33 * ;] 
rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), Matthieu 7:17-18 12:33 Luc 6:43; of fish, Matthieu 13:48. 
Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., Éphésiens 4:29. "In Hellenistic . . . it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.†

G4551.def:
Σαπφείρα, -ης (see B1., § 3, 4), ἡ 
(Aram. שַׁפִּירָא) 
Sapphia: Actes 5:1.†

G4552.def:
σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ 
[in LXX for סַפִּיר ;] 
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Apocalypse 21:19.†

G4553.def:
σαργάνη, -ης, ἡ 
__1. a plaited rope (Æsch.). 
__2. a hamper, a basket made of ropes: 2 Corinthiens 11:33.†

G4554.def:
Σάρδεις, -εων, αἱ 
Sardis, the chief city of Lydia: Apocalypse 1:11 3:1, 4

G4556.def:
σάρδιον, -ον, τ 
[in LXX for אֹדֶם, Exode 28:17, al.; also for שֹׁהַם ;] 
the sardian stone, sard (of which carnelian is one variety): Apocalypse 4:3 21:20.†

G4557.def:
σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ 
(σάρδιον, ὄνυξ), 
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Apocalypse 21:20.†

G4558.def:
Σάρεπτα, -ων (Ob 20), τά (Heb. צָרְפַת), 
Sarepta, a city of Sidon: Luc 4:26.†

G4559.def:
σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ) 
(seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7) 
= Lat. carnalis, i.e. 
__(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Romains 15:27, 1 Corinthiens 9:11; 
__(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1 Corinthiens 3:3, 2 Corinthiens 1:12 10:4, 1 Pierre 2:11.†
SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Romains 7:14

G4560.def:
σάρκινος, -η, -ον
(σάρξ), [in LXX: 2 Chroniques 32:8, Eze.11:19 36:26 (בָּשָׂר), Esther 4:17, Proverbes 24:23 (Proverbes 29:27) * ;] 
= Lat. carneus (the termination -ινος denoting the substance or material of a thing; see Tr., Syn., § LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184; and for illustrations from π., see MM, xxii), of the flesh, of flesh, fleshy (Plat., Arist., Plut., al.): Romains 7:14, 1 Corinthiens 3:1, 2 Corinthiens 3:3, Hébreux 7:16. (Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except 2 Corinthiens 3:3, but the evidence is decisive against it.)†
SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v

G4562.def:
Σερούχ (Rec. Σαρ-), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. שְׂרוּג), 
Serug: Luc 3:35.†

G4563.def:
σαρόω, -ῶ 
late form of σαίρω, 
to sweep: with accusative, Luc 15:8; pass., Matthieu 12:44, Luc 11:25.†

G4564.def:
Σάρρα, -ας, ἡ (Heb. שָׂרָה, Genèse 17:15), 
Sarah: Romains 4:19 9:9, Hébreux 11:11, 1 Pierre 3:6.†

G4565.def:
Σάρων, -ωνος (accusative -ῶνα, WH), ὁ (Heb. שָׁרוֹן), 
the plain of Sharon: Actes 9:35.†

G4567.def:
Σατανᾶς, -ᾶ
(so also Sir 21:30, but in 3Ki.11:14, σατάν indecl.; Heb. שָׂטָן; Aram. סָטָנָא, whence the inflected Gk. form), ό, 
Satan (i.e. the adversary, as in LXX, ll. with): Matthieu 4:10 12:26, Marc 1:13 3:23, 26 4:15 Luc 10:18 11:18 13:16 22:3, 31, Jean 13:27, Actes 5:3 26:18, Romains 16:20, 1 Corinthiens 5:5 7:5, 2 Corinthiens 2:11 11:14, 1 Thessaloniciens 2:18, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:9, 1 Timothée 1:20 5:15, Apocalypse 2:9, 13 2:24 3:9 12:9 20:2, 7; addressed in person of Peter, Matthieu 16:23 Marc 8:33; ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, 2 Corinthiens 12:7.†

G4568.def:
σάτον, -ου, τό
(Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Aggée 2:17 (16)* ;] 
a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Matthieu 13:33, Luc 13:21.†

G4569G.def:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see), 
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Actes 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9.†

G4569H.def:
Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see), 
Saul, the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul: Actes 7:58 8:1, 3 9:1, 8 9:11, 22 9:24 11:25, 30 12:25 13:1-2, 7 13:9.†

G4570.def:
σβέννυμι 
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבָה ;] 
of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, Matthieu 12:20, Éphésiens 6:16, Hébreux 11:34; pass., Matthieu 25:8, Marc 9:48, [44, 46]. Metaphorical (cf. Cantique des cantiques 8:7, 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:19.†
ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, 1 Thessaloniciens 5:19 T (see WH, Notes, 148).†

G4573.def:
σεβάζομαι
(σέβας, reverential awe), [in Aq.: Osée 10:5 * ;] 
__1. to fear (Hom). 
__2. In later writers, = σέβομαι, to worship: Romains 1:25

G4574.def:
σέβασμα, -τος, τό
(σεβάζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.14:20 15:17, Da TH Bel 1:27 * ;] 
an object of worship: Actes 17:23, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:4.†

G4576.def:
σέβω 
[in LXX (chiefly for יָרֵא, Josué 4:24, al.) and NT always mid., σέβομαι, exc. 4Ma.5:24 ;] 
to worship: with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 15:9, Marc 7:7, Actes 18:13 19:27; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, Actes 16:14 18:7; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, Actes 13:43, 50 17:4, 17 (cf. προσήλυτος).†

G4577.def:
σειρά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Juges 16:13-14, 19 (מַחְלָפָה), Proverbes 5:22 (חֶבֶל) * ;] 
__1. (a) a cord; 
__(b) a chain (cf. Pr., l.with): σειραὶ ζόφου, 2 Pierre 2:4, Rec., R, mg. (see: σειρός). 
__2. a lock of hair (Jg, ll. with).†

G4578.def:
σεισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(σείω), [in LXX chiefly for רַעַשׁ ;] 
a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: Matthieu 8:24; esp. an earthquake: Matthieu 24:7 27:54 28:2, Marc 13:8, Luc 21:11, Actes 16:26, Apocalypse 6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18.†

G4579.def:
σείω 
[in LXX chiefly for רָעַשׁ ;] 
to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, Hébreux 12:26 (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, Matthieu 27:51 (LXX); συκῆ, Apocalypse 6:13. Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: Matthieu 21:10 28:4 (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).†

G4581.def:
Σελευκία (Rec. -εύκεια), 
Seleucia, a city of Syria: Actes 13:4.†

G4582.def:
σελήνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵחַ (Genèse 37:9, al.), also for לְבָנָה; (Cantique des cantiques 6:9(10), ?Ésaïe 24:23 30:26) ;] 
the moon: Matthieu 24:29, Marc 13:24, Luc 21:25, Actes 2:20" (LXX), 1 Corinthiens 15:41, Apocalypse 6:12 8:12 12:1 21:23.†

G4583.def:
σεληνιάζω
(σελήνη), 
act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι, 
to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): Matthieu 4:24 17:15.†

G4584.def:
Σεμεείν (Rec. Σεμεΐ), ὁ, indecl., 
Semein: Luc 3:26.†

G4585.def:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;] 
fine wheaten flour: Apocalypse 18:13.†

G4586.def:
σεμνός, -ή, -όν 
(σέβομαι), [in LXX: Proverbes 6:8 8:6 15:26, 2Ma.6:11 2Mac 6:28 2Mac 8:15, 4Ma.5:36 4Mac 7:15 4Mac 17:5 * ;] 
__1. reverend, august, venerable, in cl. of the gods and also of human beings. 
__2. grave, serious; of persons: 1 Timothée 3:8 3:11, Tite 2:2; of things: Philippiens 4:8 (see Tr., Syn., § xcii; Cremer, 37; MM, xxii).†

G4587.def:
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] 
gravity: 1 Timothée 2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tite 2:7.†

G4588.def:
Σέργιος, -ου, ὁ 
Sergius, surnamed Paulus: Actes 13:7.†

G4589.def:
Σήθ, ὁ (Heb. שֵׁת), 
indecl., 
Seth (Genèse 4:25): Luc 3:38.†

G4590.def:
Σήμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֵׁם), 
Shem: Luc 3:36.†

G4591.def:
σημαίνω
(σῆμα, a sign), [in LXX for רוּעַ hi., תָּקַע, etc. ;] 
to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), Actes 25:27, Apocalypse 1:1 (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., Actes 11:28; before quæst. indir., Jean 12:33 18:32 21:19.†

G4593.def:
σημειόω, -ῶ
(σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psaumes 4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] 
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2 Thessaloniciens 3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†

G4594.def:
σήμερον (Att.. τήμερον), 
adv., [in LXX for יוֹם ;] 
to-day: Matthieu 6:11, Luc 4:21, Actes 4:9, al.; opposite to αὔριον, Matthieu 6:30, Luc 12:28, Jacques 4:13; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, Hébreux 13:8; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, Actes 20:20; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, Romains 11:8, 2 Corinthiens 3:14; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), Matthieu 11:23 27:8; as subst., τὸ σ., Hébreux 3:13; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., Hébreux 4:7 R, mg., (see Westc., in l)

G4595.def:
σήπω 
[in LXX; Psaumes 38:5 (מָקַק ni.), Job 33:21 (כָּלָה) Job 40:7, Sir.14:19, al. ;] 
to make corrupt: 2 pf. act, with mid, sense (see M, Pr., 154), σέσηπεν, has perished, become corrupted, Jacques 5:2.†

G4596.def:
σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν 
(οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk), 
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Apocalypse 18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†

G4597.def:
σής σητός (late genitive for cl. σεός), ὁ, 
[in LXX: Job 4:19, Ésaïe 50:9 (עָשׁ), Ésaïe 51:8 (סָס), al. ;]
